description.purpose: Composite agent: one hive that references session-keeper@2.2.0, collector@4.0.0 and dispatcher@1.2.0 as sub-units plus an llm brain slot, with every internal edge pre-wired -- the stamp promotion, the seam into the brain, the dispatcher lanes, the loopback with restore_ttl and its iteration bound, the close path and the write fan-out. Since 4.3.0 (GH #447) the composite no longer carries a summarizer: the close batch leaves on the write port, the member above it turns that into the memory hive's close pass, and what the next generation needs of the last one comes back through the recall bundle rather than through a system.handover return. The topology the Egon rollout wired by hand, as one add_nodes. Since 4.2.0 (GH #55) one more internal edge belongs to it: the tool this composite IMPLEMENTS -- thread_recall, answered by the collector inside it out of a slate no other cell may read -- is routed from the dispatcher to the collector by this template's own graph, and the tool exit towards the caller became a guarded default edge (GH #283) that stays silent for exactly the names an ordinary edge already claimed. `memory_recall` was the second such name from 4.2.0 to 4.6.1 and is an ORDINARY tool name since 5.0.0 ([#552](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/552)): the memory belongs to the MEMBER, so the member's own memory hive declares the schema and answers the call, and this composite lets it leave on the tool exit like any other name. Since 4.4.0 ([#458](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/458)) the composite carries the lane its own seal made impossible: `in_pack`, from the hive path through the collector into the brain, where a pack of durable `system.*` slots becomes an upsert into the brain's own `cell.db`. It needed `collector@3.2.0`, it cost two internal edges and one folded-in door term, and it answers every pack on `pack_ack` -- a paired lane, like the prune. A new accepted lane and a new emitted one is the second digit (`docs/development-rules.md` § 4/4a); nothing that shipped changed behaviour. Since `4.5.0` ([#464](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/464)) the composite also stops carrying a tool menu somebody typed. `./collector`'s `params.tools` is the list of names this agent DECLARES it uses -- `["web_search", "web_fetch"]` as shipped -- the names leave on `schemas` for a tools hive's `in_schemas` door, and the declarations come back on `in_menu` and are written into the brain as durable `system.tools`. One write per change and nothing per turn; a name the hive has nothing under comes back in `hop.menu_unknown` and as a warn line rather than as a silence. It needs `collector@3.3.0`, one more cell and three internal edges. A new accepted lane and a new emitted one is again the second digit. Since `4.5.0` ([#475](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/475)) it also passes the transfer lanes of the keeper it holds straight through: `in_export` and `in_import` in, `dump` out, three plain edges and no modifier, because the lane is named the same on both sides of this boundary. The keeper has answered those lanes since `session-keeper@2.2.0` and nothing above it forwarded one, so the sessions -- the table that decides whether a conversation continues or starts at zero -- stayed behind on every rebuild. A new accepted lane and a new emitted one is again the second digit; `4.5.0` has not shipped, so it is extended rather than superseded. 4.5.1 re-points the collector ref at the collector whose menu is merged over several answerers ([#529](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/529)). Standalone this composite has exactly one -- a tools hive -- and behaves as 4.5.0 did; the second answerer appears one level up, where an `assistant` stands this surface beside a reasoning core and declares the errand that core answers. Since 4.6.0 the rim declares the two halves of the CREDENTIAL LANE and names `./brain` as their connect point (GH #560): `emits.credential_request` and `accepts.in_sealed`, both carrying `at: ["./brain"]`. That lets the member level draw the lane as a v-lane (GH #559) straight from the brain to the person's own `access`, instead of a pass-through chain through three rims -- and it lets a brain run on `params.credential_grant_id` with no key in its config at all. A caller can now dock something it could never dock before, so it is the second digit (docs/development-rules.md § 4/4a). Since 4.6.1 the collector ref carries the partial answer (GH #570): a round of this composite that spends its iteration budget now ends on a named partial answer with `hop.partial` beside `hop.round_capped`, instead of on the raw end of the tool round. Only the pin moves -- no lane, no port, no param of this template. Since 5.0.0 the menu is re-asked on the MUTATION RECEIPT rather than on a five-minute tick (GH #553): the composite declares `mutation_committed` at its own rim -- the lane keeps ONE name from the mutation door down to the collector -- and carries it inwards with one edge of its own. The collector's `menu-clock` is gone. Since 5.0.0 every behaviour knob of this composite is a PARAM of the cell that reads it -- the collector's since `collector@1.2.0`, the keeper's since `session-keeper@2.2.0`, the dispatcher's since `dispatcher@1.2.0`, and the brain's `credential_grant_id` as a literal empty string here ([#138](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/138), ruling R-0904-6). What stays in `.env` is the provider lane: the API key, the endpoint and the model id.
description.use_when: Whenever a colony needs a conversational agent that remembers its own session: a chat surface, a phone line, an operator console. Instantiate via add_nodes AND wire the four ports via add_edges IN THE SAME MUTATION - the composite is edge-connected from apply on (no island dance). Instantiation needs ctx.model (a RESOLVED literal, K-H2 lane B).
description.not_in_scope: No tool cells - the tool set is the per-agent choice and its lanes are wired per instance on hop.tool_name. ONE exception since 4.2.0 (GH #55), and it is a boundary rather than a gap: the tool this composite IMPLEMENTS -- thread_recall, served by the collector inside it out of the round table in its own cell.db -- is routed by this template's own edge and needs no wiring from the parent. `memory_recall` was the second until 5.0.0 and is the parent's now (#552): the member's memory hive declares and answers it, the call leaves on the tool exit, and the four member edges plus the six of the assistant level are what carry it -- a tool the composite implements is topology, a tool somebody else answers is wiring. A tool the composite implements is topology; a tool the parent wires is the agent. No memory hive, no surface proxy, no drain cell, no persona: the write target, the recall port, the reply sink and where errors land are all the parent tree's decision. And `in_pack` is not an open write channel into the prompt: four slot names (`identity`, `persona`, `handover`, `instructions` since [#488](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/488)), checked against a constant in the collector, owner off the envelope. Who may OPEN such a lane is decided one level further out -- the edge is a mutation, and `templates/submit` checks its form while the broker answers the capability `affinity.subscribe` (GH #458). And no tool SCHEMAS of the parent's tools: since 4.5.0 the composite asks for them, which is not the same as owning them -- what it owns is the DECLARATION (`params.tools`), and the declarations themselves live in the tools hive beside the cells they describe (GH #464).
examples: PORTS - every endpoint is the composite's own path (`params.ports` is empty since GH #228; an edge naming ./session-keeper, ./collector, ./dispatcher, ./brain or ./errors is refused with hive_port_boundary), and what a caller wants rides on hop.route -- the door edges in here decide which cell that means. Ingress: that path, lane in_turn (the parent edge MUST promote the channel identity to context.channel, otherwise every chat lands on the channel 'default'). Reply exit: the same path on hop.route=='answer' (THREE sorts: a real answer, a round that hit max_iter told apart by hop.round_capped, and -- since collector@2.1.1 -- a turn that could not be assembled at all because the store refused a read or a write, told apart by hop.degraded, which such a message carries INSTEAD of round_capped. A reply edge guarded on round_capped alone lets the third through and reads a store refusal to a person as a real answer, so guard on both; GH #343). Write exit: the same path on hop.route=='write' (the closed session as one batch; the target is the parent's choice), and the same path on hop.route=='turn_write' - ONE finished turn per message and never a batch (GH #298, ruling Q11): one user/assistant turn in messages[], hop.turn_id '<session_id>#<index>', hop.turn_index and hop.happened_at beside it, which is the shape a memory hive's episode lane reads, so a memory behind it is fresh per turn. On unless params.turn_write is set to '' or '0'. It is NOT the same target as 'write': that route carries a closed day for whoever archives one, and wiring both into one memory would be a second writer over turns this lane already wrote. Error drain: the same path on hop.route=='error' (MUST be wired). Per instance: the same path on hop.route=='tool' && hop.tool_name=='<name>' out to each tool cell, and every tool cell back into that same path with route in_tool. Optional: the recall / in_bundle pair for a memory hive, in_sweep, and the two operator lanes of the context window, in_prune and in_round_sweep. Transfer, since 4.5.0 (GH #475): the same path on in_export and on in_import, both crossing untouched to the keeper inside, and the same path on hop.route == 'export_done' (the keeper wrote its own ledger and says where, GH #555) and hop.route == 'dump' (the receipt of one applied import part). BOTH are PAIRED in required_drains (in_export -> export_done, in_import -> dump), and each drain edge must be a PLAIN hop.route test -- one that additionally tested a second hop key evaluates false under the drain probe and reads as no drain at all. A porter refusal does NOT travel that lane: it is normalised by the composite's own error cell and leaves on the error drain beside every other failure of the unit. in_prune is PAIRED (since 3.0.6): it answers unconditionally -- with what it cut or with a zero report saying nothing was eligible -- on hop.route=='prune', and required_drains refuses a mutation that wires the ingress without a plain subscription to the report. RETRACTED in 4.2.0 (GH #55): until 4.1.1 this paragraph told the caller to wire the tools the composite serves ITSELF -- a loop at the composite's own path, hop.tool_name=='thread_recall' back in on lane in_thread_call. There is NOTHING left to wire for it, and a caller that still draws that edge gets a DOUBLE delivery of every such call, so remove it when you lift an instance to 4.2.0. The lane stays declared and stays a real door at that same path -- a caller MAY still hand such a call in on it -- but nothing obliges it to. `memory_recall` was the second name until 5.0.0 (GH #552) and is an ORDINARY tool name now: it leaves on the tool exit and the PARENT routes it to a memory that declares and answers it, which is why the lane in_memory_call is gone from this contract. How the composite answers them is not a caller's address: see description.purpose and the README. The sub-units in here are sealed hives of their own, and for a caller that changes nothing: they are INTERIOR to this composite, which is sealed too, so an endpoint naming one of them -- or reaching past it, as in ./session-keeper/stamp or ./collector/assemble -- is refused with hive_port_boundary all the same. Which cell inside picks a message up is decided by the in_ lane the edge sets, by the door edges in here, and that is what lets the inside of a sub-unit change without touching a caller.

model.because: the model the brain infers with — a RESOLVED literal, K-H2 lane B
